title: Gym&I supported exercise catalog

scope.purpose: Selectable movements for a general fitness demo planner and their supported vision variations.
excluded_uses: Automatic selection of a user's training load

sources.title: ACSM Position Stand: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults
supports: Progressive resistance training benefits healthy adults.
At least two sets per exercise is a reasonable baseline; strength benefits are associated with 2-3 sets and at least two weekly sessions.
Hypertrophy benefits are associated with higher weekly volume (at least about 10 sets per muscle group per week); increase volume gradually.
Training to momentary failure is not required. Sets can use a near-failure effort such as roughly 2-3 repetitions in reserve.
Specific equipment, tempo, and periodization are not uniquely required for the average healthy adult.

sources.title: ACSM: 5 Things to Know About Creating an Effective Resistance Training Plan
supports: Train all major muscle groups at least two days per week and build gradually.
For strength, heavier loads around 80% of one-repetition maximum and 2-3 sets are highlighted.
For hypertrophy, higher weekly volume around 10 sets per muscle group is highlighted.

sources.title: CDC: Adult Activity Recommendations
supports: Adults should do muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days per week that works all major muscle groups.

sources.title: ACE Exercise Library: Triceps Extension
supports: A two-handed overhead dumbbell triceps-extension setup and controlled movement description.

sources.title: ACE Exercise Library: Bent-over Row
supports: Hip-hinged row setup and back-position coaching considerations.

strength_days_per_week.recommended_for: healthy adults; distribute work across the week

effort.load_policy: The user chooses or confirms the load. Do not estimate a safe load from pose, heart rate, or model output.

progression.rule: Build gradually. If the user completes every prescribed set at the top of the rep range with controlled movement and reports that the load feels manageable, suggest a small available increase for the user to confirm.

rest_policy.note: The current ACSM evidence review did not establish one optimal rest interval for everyone. These are adjustable planning defaults: allow more recovery for heavy or demanding sets, and extend rest when the user is not ready to maintain controlled movement.

programming_defaults.warm_up: Offer a brief general warm-up and, when useful, lighter practice repetitions before work sets. Do not make an exact warm-up duration a health requirement.
programming_defaults.stop_rule: Stop the set and session for pain or dizziness; do not coach the user to push through.

fitness.description: Simple, manageable starting prescription for general fitness.
fitness.load: User-confirmed resistance that permits controlled repetitions; bodyweight when specified.
fitness.effort: Aim to finish with about 2-3 good repetitions still possible; this is a practical effort cue, not a precise measurement.

muscle_growth.description: Use multiple sets and track weekly work for each muscle group; build volume progressively rather than starting at a high volume.
muscle_growth.load: User-confirmed resistance that permits controlled repetitions.
muscle_growth.effort: Aim to finish with about 2-3 good repetitions still possible; do not require momentary failure.

strength_building.description: Prioritize strength-focused movements early in the session and give demanding sets enough recovery.
strength_building.load: User-confirmed. ACSM highlights heavier loads around 80% 1RM for strength, but Gym&I does not test or infer 1RM; do not apply this percentage unless a qualified plan already supplies it.
strength_building.effort: Use challenging but controlled repetitions; stop before technique breaks down.

exercises.camera_guidance: Front view; keep the shoulder, elbow, and wrist of the working arm visible.
setup_and_coaching: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and alternate arms.
Use a load the user confirms they can control; keep the torso steady and lower each weight under control.
limitations: Repetition target is per arm; UI and backend should avoid presenting alternating left-plus-right movements as one rep unless that counting convention is explicitly chosen.

exercises.camera_guidance: Side view for the current analyzer; keep hip, knee, and ankle visible.
setup_and_coaching: Use a clear, stable area and a comfortable stance.
Descend only through a comfortable range and stand back up with control; do not force depth or coach through pain.
limitations: Only the bodyweight variation is included; do not relabel a loaded squat as this analyzed exercise.

exercises.camera_guidance: Front or slight front-oblique view; keep both arms visible throughout the press.
setup_and_coaching: Stand with a stable stance and one dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level.
Press through a comfortable overhead range without forcing the shoulders or leaning back; lower with control.
limitations: Do not treat the pose model as a shoulder-pain or injury screen.

exercises.camera_guidance: Side or front-oblique view; keep shoulder, elbow, and wrist visible.
setup_and_coaching: Hold one dumbbell securely with both hands overhead.
Bend and extend the elbows smoothly through a comfortable range; keep the torso stable and do not force the bottom position.
limitations: Requires a secure two-handed grip and enough overhead clearance.

exercises.camera_guidance: Side or slight oblique view; keep shoulder, elbow, and wrist visible.
setup_and_coaching: Hold dumbbells, hinge at the hips, and keep a stable, comfortable torso position.
Pull the elbows back under control and lower the weights smoothly; do not use momentum or force a hinge depth.
limitations: A bent-over position may not suit every user; honor stated movement restrictions and do not diagnose back safety from camera pose.

exercises.camera_guidance: Side view; keep shoulder, elbow, and wrist visible.
setup_and_coaching: Start in the standard plank position on a stable surface with hands under or slightly wider than the shoulders.
Lower and press through a comfortable range while maintaining a steady body position; stop if pain occurs.
limitations: Incline, knee, and weighted variations are not included because the supported model variation is standard push-up; do not claim live analysis for an untrained variation.

exercises.camera_guidance: Front view; keep shoulder and hip landmarks visible.
setup_and_coaching: Stand tall holding one light, user-confirmed dumbbell at the side.
Move slowly through a small comfortable side bend and return upright; avoid twisting or leaning forward/back.
limitations: This movement covers lateral trunk flexion only; it does not represent complete abdominal or core training.
Honor user-stated back or trunk restrictions; the model does not assess injury risk.

exercises.camera_guidance: Side view; keep hip, knee, and ankle visible. The camera cannot assess spinal curvature, bracing, bar load, or injury risk.
setup_and_coaching: Use a clear lifting area and a barbell with user-confirmed plates.
Begin with the bar close to the body and lift smoothly; use a load and range the user can control.
Do not treat the model's rep count or relative movement observations as proof of safe technique.
limitations: The model analyzes conventional deadlift only when this variation is selected.
Do not infer or recommend a starting load; user confirms load.
Romanian deadlift is a rejection example, not a selectable catalog exercise.

exercises.camera_guidance: Side view for the current analyzer; keep hip, knee, and ankle visible. Side view does not capture all technique details.
setup_and_coaching: Use a clear lifting area and a barbell with user-confirmed plates.
Select a stance the user has practiced and can control; lift smoothly without forcing stance width or range.
Do not treat the model's rep count or relative movement observations as proof of safe technique.
limitations: The model's hip-angle counter needs validation on sumo footage before live rep counts or form cues are presented as reliable.
Do not infer or recommend a starting load; user confirms load.
Romanian deadlift is a rejection example, not a selectable catalog exercise.

recognition_rejection_examples.name: Romanian deadlift
recognition_rejection_examples.reason: Use as a negative/reject example for the supported conventional and sumo deadlift classes; it is not a selectable exercise or deadlift variation in this catalog.

coverage_notes: This is a list of model-supported demo movements, not a complete weekly program for all major muscle groups.
The set does not include a dedicated calf exercise or a complete trunk/core program.
Do not describe a plan built only from this catalog as a complete balanced program unless the missing coverage is addressed.
